items.informal_name: Cardinality of (n+1)-th Disjointed Interval in Product Type
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [inst : Ring α] [inst_1 : PartialOrder α] [IsOrderedRing α] [inst_3 : Ring β]
  [inst_4 : PartialOrder β] [IsOrderedRing β] [inst_6 : LocallyFiniteOrder α] [inst_7 : LocallyFiniteOrder β]
  [inst_8 : DecidableEq α] [inst_9 : DecidableEq β] [inst_10 : DecidableLE (α × β)] (n : ℕ),
  (Finset.box (n + 1)).card =
    (Finset.Icc (-↑n.succ) ↑n.succ).card * (Finset.Icc (-↑n.succ) ↑n.succ).card -
      (Finset.Icc (-↑n) ↑n).card * (Finset.Icc (-↑n) ↑n).card
items.informal_description: For any natural number $n$, the cardinality of the $(n+1)$-th disjointed interval $\text{box}(n+1)$ in the product type $\alpha \times \beta$ satisfies: $$\#(\text{box}(n+1)) = \#([-n-1, n+1]_\alpha) \cdot \#([-n-1, n+1]_\beta) - \#([-n, n]_\alpha) \cdot \#([-n, n]_\beta),$$ where $[-k, k]_\gamma$ denotes the closed interval $\{x \in \gamma \mid -k \le x \le k\}$ for $\gamma \in \{\alpha, \beta\}$.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of $[a, b)$ in Product Type: $\prod_i (|[a_i, b_i]| - 1)$
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_2} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_2 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (α i)]
  [inst_3 : (i : ι) → PartialOrder (α i)] [inst_4 : (i : ι) → LocallyFiniteOrder (α i)] (a b : (i : ι) → α i),
  (Finset.Ico a b).card = ∏ i, (Finset.Icc (a i) (b i)).card - 1
items.informal_description: For a product type equipped with a locally finite order, the cardinality of the half-open interval $[a, b)$ is equal to the product over all indices $i$ of $(|[a_i, b_i]| - 1)$, where $[a_i, b_i]$ denotes the closed interval in the $i$-th component.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Product Interval: $\#([a, b]) = \prod_i \#([a_i, b_i])$
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_2} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_2 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (α i)]
  [inst_3 : (i : ι) → PartialOrder (α i)] [inst_4 : (i : ι) → LocallyFiniteOrder (α i)] (a b : (i : ι) → α i),
  (Finset.Icc a b).card = ∏ i, (Finset.Icc (a i) (b i)).card
items.informal_description: For a product type $\prod_{i : \iota} \alpha(i)$ with a finite index type $\iota$ and each component $\alpha(i)$ equipped with a locally finite order, the cardinality of the closed interval $[a, b]$ is equal to the product of the cardinalities of the component-wise closed intervals $[a_i, b_i]$. Formally, $\#(\mathrm{Icc}\, a\, b) = \prod_{i} \#(\mathrm{Icc}\, (a_i)\, (b_i))$.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Product Interval Equals Product of Component Cardinalities
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_2} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_2 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (α i)]
  [inst_3 : (i : ι) → Lattice (α i)] [inst_4 : (i : ι) → LocallyFiniteOrder (α i)] (a b : (i : ι) → α i),
  (Finset.uIcc a b).card = ∏ i, (Finset.uIcc (a i) (b i)).card
items.informal_description: For a product type $\prod_{i : \iota} \alpha(i)$ where $\iota$ is a finite index type and each component $\alpha(i)$ has a locally finite order, the cardinality of the unordered interval $[a, b]$ is equal to the product of the cardinalities of the component-wise intervals $[a(i), b(i)]$ for each $i \in \iota$. Formally, $\#(\text{uIcc}\, a\, b) = \prod_{i} \#(\text{uIcc}\, (a(i))\, (b(i)))$.
